title: Browse the tree as a static page
description: A project owner opens a static browsable page of the whole RCF tree locally, with each document shown as readable text and inter-document links navigating between sections.
iWant: a browsable static page of the whole tree that I can open locally
soThat: I can read each document's content and follow its links without a server or a JSON viewer

acceptanceCriteria.description: The view serves a live page from a local server process and writes no files
acceptanceCriteria.then: a valid HTML5 page is served live by a local server process and no files are written to disk

acceptanceCriteria.description: Each document's key fields are rendered as readable text, not raw JSON
acceptanceCriteria.then: its key fields are rendered as readable text, not raw JSON
the link navigates to that document's section

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] The audit view header keeps every main tab visible and the .tools group right of them at any viewport the chrome supports: the tablist and .tools cannot shrink below their intrinsic width (flex-shrink: 0) and .product carries the shrink budget via min-width: 0 (both on the flex item and on .product .name) so the project name ellipsizes first.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the viewer rendered in the standalone (non-embed) shell
acceptanceCriteria.when: any viewport >= 721px the chrome supports (above the responsive @media that re-rows the tabs under 720px)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the six main tabs are fully visible and the .tools group sits right of them; .product .name ellipsizes when the project name is longer than its slot and nothing in .tools overlaps a clipped tab

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] The .product .name span carries a title="<full name>" attribute so hovering reveals the whole name when the ellipsis has clipped it; the title is HTML-escaped on the same path as the inner text, and when the product block collapses (no project name on the tree) no title attribute is emitted.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project tree with a projectName
acceptanceCriteria.then: the .name span has title="<the full projectName>" with the same HTML-escaping as the inner text

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] The header display name prefers prd.productName, then manifest.projectName, then prd.productTitle. A rename via `rcf define update PRD-001 --set productName=...` therefore reaches the audit chrome without touching manifest.projectName (which the chain keeps for ids and paths).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a tree where both manifest.projectName and prd.productName are set
acceptanceCriteria.then: the header projectName is prd.productName; when the PRD carries no productName the fallback is manifest.projectName, then prd.productTitle
